# Fixture provenance

Per `docs/06_CONVENTIONS.md`: every PDF in `tests/fixtures/` must have
documented provenance. No mystery PDFs.

| File | Origin | Why it's here |
|---|---|---|
| `basic/hello.pdf` | Hand-constructed in `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-hello.py` (run once, committed). Minimal valid PDF 1.4, US Letter, single page rendering "Hello, VibePDF." in built-in Helvetica. ~400 bytes. | Smoke-test fixture: proves PDFium and PDF.js can each open *something*. No fonts to embed, no encryption, no annotations. |
| `golden/hello-p0-72dpi.png` | **Self-generated** render of `basic/hello.pdf` page 0 at 72 DPI (612×792, 8-bit RGBA), produced by *our own* PDFium pipeline via the `bless_goldens` test in `src-tauri/tests/render_compare.rs`. **Not** a reference render from an independent PDF reader. | Regression baseline for the P1.E2 render-fidelity scaffold (P1-VIEW-004). The gate test `renders_match_goldens` compares fresh renders against it within tolerance and logs divergences to `tests/render-failures.md`. Regenerate after an intentional renderer change with `cargo test ... -- --ignored bless_goldens`. |
| `basic/links.pdf` | Hand-constructed in `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-links.py` (run once, committed). Minimal valid PDF 1.4, **3** US-Letter pages; page 1 has a `/Link` annotation whose `/Dest` references page 3's *object* (`5 0 R`). ~1.3 KB. | P2-PAGE-003 reference-integrity fixture. `src-tauri/tests/delete_page.rs` deletes page 2 and asserts the page-1 link still targets page 3 (now index 1) — proving surviving object-ref destinations track renumbering. |
| `basic/many-pages.pdf` | Hand-constructed in `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-many.py` (run once, committed). Minimal valid PDF 1.4, **50** US-Letter pages, each rendering "Page N" in built-in Helvetica. ~13.5 KB. | P4-EDIT-009 watermark acceptance ("DRAFT on a 50-page PDF in <2s") in `src-tauri/tests/watermark.rs`; a generic multi-page fixture for Track D's later page-decoration features (header/footer, page numbers, Bates). |
| `basic/rotated.pdf` | Hand-constructed in `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-rotated.py` (run once, committed). PDF 1.4, **4** US-Letter pages with `/Rotate` 0/90/180/270, each rendering "Rotate N". ~1.4 KB. | P4.HF (FABLE_REVIEW 3.1): decoration writers must compensate for page rotation; per-angle matrix tests in the watermark / background / header-footer suites. |
| `basic/cropped.pdf` | Hand-constructed in `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-cropped.py` (run once, committed). PDF 1.4, one page with `/CropBox [100 100 512 692]` inside `/MediaBox [0 0 612 792]`. ~0.6 KB. | P4.HF (FABLE_REVIEW 3.4): decoration *placement* targets the visible CropBox; the background colour fill still covers the MediaBox. |
| `basic/ccitt.pdf` | Hand-constructed in `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-ccitt.py` (run once, committed). PDF 1.4, one 160×160 pt page painting a 16×16 `/DeviceGray` 1-bit image compressed `/CCITTFaxDecode` `/K 0`, encoded by the script from the ITU-T T.4 terminating-code tables. Pattern: black at rows 2–5 × columns 1–10 and rows 9–13 × columns 8–14. ~0.8 KB. Checked independently: Ghostscript renders every pixel as the pattern. | P1-VIEW-004: `src/view/__tests__/image-decoders.test.ts` proves PDF.js's `jbig2.wasm` (shared by JBIG2 and CCITT) loads from the served `public/pdfjs/wasm/` and decodes to the pattern. |
| `basic/jpx.pdf` | Built by `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-jpx.py` (run once, committed), which encodes a 16×16 RGB pattern losslessly with **OpenJPEG's `opj_compress`** (`-n 3`) and wraps the raw codestream as `/JPXDecode`. Quadrants: red, green / blue, white. ~1 KB. Byte-identical per OpenJPEG version. Checked independently: Ghostscript renders every pixel as the pattern. | P1-VIEW-004: the same test for `openjpeg.wasm`. |
| `basic/scan.pdf` | Built by `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-scan.py` (run once, committed): it lays out four lines of Helvetica (24 pt heading, three 9 pt body lines) in a temporary PDF, rasterises that page to 8-bit grayscale at **150 DPI** with **Ghostscript**, and embeds the raster as the page's only content. ~5.9 KB, 1275x1650 px. No text objects, so text extraction yields nothing. 150 DPI is deliberate: below P7-OCR-003's 300 DPI floor, so the upscale stage runs. | P7-OCR-001/003: `src-tauri/tests/ocr_smoke.rs` reads it with Tesseract and checks the words, their boxes and the line structure. The 9 pt lines are what catch a preprocessing stage that erodes strokes — the first denoise implementation turned "brown" into "broval" and only small text exposed it. |
| `basic/scan-rotated.pdf` | Same generator as `scan.pdf`, with the raster turned 90° clockwise onto a 792×612 page carrying `/Rotate 270`, so it *displays* exactly like `scan.pdf` while its ink sits sideways in page space. ~7 KB. | P7-OCR-001: the OCR text layer has to be written in the page's own space, not the displayed one. An earlier version of this fixture displayed *sideways* (upright ink + `/Rotate 90`) — no scanner produces that, and Tesseract read nothing from it, which is why the rotation moved into the raster. |
| `basic/scan-skewed.pdf` | Same generator, with every line drawn through a 3° text matrix before rasterising — indistinguishable from a page fed crooked through a scanner. ~6.4 KB. | P7-OCR-001: preprocessing straightens the image for recognition, so the invisible text must be tilted back by the same angle or it drifts off the ink. This fixture caught the sign being inverted. |
| `basic/scan-cyrillic.pdf` | Built by the ignored test `writes_the_cyrillic_scan_fixture` in `src-tauri/src/pdf/ocr_text_layer.rs`: two Cyrillic lines ("Счёт номер 4821", "документ от 14 марта") set in a **system face found on the build machine** via VibePDF's CID embedding, rasterised at 150 DPI by PDFium, then re-embedded as the page's only content. ~9 KB. Rust rather than Python because Ghostscript's base fonts cannot set Cyrillic at all. The face used depends on the machine, so regenerating it may change the bytes — it is committed for that reason. | P7-OCR-002: `src-tauri/tests/ocr_languages.rs` OCRs it in Russian and reads the words back out. Cyrillic is outside WinAnsi, so it is the fixture that proves the text layer embeds a font instead of silently dropping the words. |
| `basic/two-column.pdf` | Hand-constructed in `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-two-column.py` (run once, committed). One US-Letter page, two columns of five Helvetica lines ("Alpha one…", "Beta one…"), drawn **interleaved** — left line 1, right line 1, left line 2 — which is what page-layout tools commonly emit. ~1 KB. | P7-OCR-006: the fixture that fails when text is concatenated in content-stream order. Measured 2026-09-23: PDFium's own `text().all()` returns "Alpha one Beta one\r\nAlpha two Beta two", i.e. the columns merged line by line, which is why `pdf::export_text` rebuilds the order from geometry instead. |
| `basic/unicode-text.pdf` | Built by the ignored test `writes_the_unicode_text_fixture` in `src-tauri/src/pdf/export_text.rs`: three lines of Cyrillic, Greek and accented Latin set in a **system face found on the build machine** via VibePDF's CID embedding. ~330 KB, nearly all of it the embedded font. Rust rather than Python because the base-14 fonts cannot encode these scripts. The face depends on the machine, so regenerating may change the bytes. | P7-OCR-006's "emit Unicode UTF-8": `src-tauri/tests/export_text.rs` exports it and reads the file back as UTF-8, checking the words survive. A lossy encoding path turns these into `?` and fails. |
| `basic/noisy-scan.pdf` | **Gitignored — generated, not committed.** Built by `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-noisy-scan.py`: 20 pages of `many-pages.pdf` rasterised to 8-bit grayscale at 300 DPI with Ghostscript, then given per-pixel sensor noise (±14 levels, fixed seed) and Flate-compressed. ~81 MB at 20 pages, ~28 MB at the 6 the tests use. | P7-OCR-010: the only fixture compression can act on. `scan.pdf` is 5.9 KB of near-white page that Flate already stores better than any JPEG could — useful for proving the "never keep a bigger result" rule, useless for measuring a ratio. Noise is why real scans are large: Flate cannot model it and JPEG discards it almost free. Not committed because a fixture with that property is megabytes by nature; `src-tauri/tests/compress.rs` skips its ratio tests with a printed regenerate instruction when it is absent. |
| `basic/report.pdf` | Hand-constructed in `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-report.py` (run once, committed). One US-Letter page, PDF 1.4: three heading sizes (20/14/11 pt Helvetica-Bold) over 9 pt body, an italic line and a bold line as their own paragraphs, and a 64×48 `DeviceRGB` image drawn at 128×96 pt. ~7 KB. | P7-OCR-004: the only fixture with all four things a Word conversion must preserve. Three heading *sizes* so levels can be told apart rather than merely detected; real `Helvetica-Bold`/`-Oblique` so the converter has font names and flags to read; and — deliberately — `&`, `<`, `>` and `"` in the prose, because the text goes straight into `document.xml` and an unescaped ampersand produces a file every reader refuses. A fixture without those characters lets that ship. |
| `basic/table.pdf` | Hand-constructed in `tests/fixtures/basic/generate-table.py` (run once, committed). Three US-Letter pages, each with the same 4-column × 4-row ruled table plus prose above and below. Page 1 draws every rule as its **own stroked line**; page 2 draws the **whole grid as one path** with many subpaths; page 3 draws it **under a `cm` transform** at half scale. Page 1 also carries two page-wide **decoy** section rules. ~4 KB. | P7-OCR-004's table clause. Three pages because a detector has to survive all three ways a grid reaches the page. Page 3 is the regression guard for the measured trap that `PDFium` reports segment points *before* the object matrix and bounds *after* — without it, a detector that ignores the matrix passes every test and mislocates every rule in a real document. The last column is plain integers on purpose: every other value carries a thousands separator or a percent sign and therefore stays text in a spreadsheet (P7-OCR-008), so without one unambiguous number the numeric-cell path would never be exercised end to end. The decoys pin the opposite failure: a section rule under a heading has no verticals and must not become a table, since a false table is worse for a reader than none. |
| `fonts/NotoSansCoptic-Regular.ttf` | **Noto Sans Coptic**, © The Noto Project Authors, redistributed under **SIL OFL 1.1** (see `fonts/OFL-NOTICE.txt`). A small (~28 KB) single-script TrueType font whose glyphs sit entirely outside the WinAnsi range. Vendored as-is. | P4.HF5 (FABLE_REVIEW 3.2 stage-2): a deterministic, offline font to exercise the PDFium font-embedding path — `font_embed.rs` and the non-WinAnsi header/footer branch embed it and assert the Coptic text round-trips through save/reopen. Not shipped in the app. |

Acceptance fixtures (`acceptance/p1-spec.pdf`, `p1-encrypted.pdf`,
`p1-large.pdf`) referenced in `docs/05_ROADMAP.md` are not yet checked
in — see Q4 in the bootstrap plan. They are generated on demand by
`python3 tests/fixtures/acceptance/generate.py` and gitignored.

`p1-encrypted.pdf` (user password `vibepdf`, owner password
`vibepdf-owner`, 256-bit AES via pypdf) is consumed by both the Phase
1 acceptance demo and by `src-tauri/tests/encrypted_open.rs`
(P1.B2 / P1-VIEW-003). The Rust test skips gracefully with a printed
regenerate instruction when the fixture is absent, so `cargo test` on
a fresh clone never silently mis-passes.
